claims.title: The nonzero type vector away from the geometric prime
claims.hypotheses: Use the odd-rank CM unitary datum and its split cuspidal type, the quadratic-generator and integral nonzero-value hypotheses, and an eligible auxiliary prime and level. Each observation is a stabilizing deck operator or an eligible spherical test.
claims.statement: The transported function is nonzero, lies in the image of the type projector and has all the observed eigenvalues with their level and central-character factors.

claims.review: The involution preserves the integral matrix group; evaluating at the involution of the original nonzero argument recovers the same value. The two finite coset normalizations were checked separately.

claims.title: Extending an eigenvector through the local compact cosets
claims.hypotheses: The function away from p is right invariant at the chosen level, fixed by the type projector, and rationally covariant for each rational element whose local component lies in the compact subgroup at p.
claims.statement: Extending by zero outside the rational orbit of the identity coset gives a nonzero definite automorphic form carrying the same simultaneous eigenvalues.

claims.title: The common vector in the definite class sum
claims.hypotheses: The initial and class representatives are equivalent definite Hermitian forms, with the prescribed adelic trivializations and rational coefficient action. The original extended form is a nonzero joint eigenvector.
claims.statement: Change of representative sends the form to a nonzero eigenvector in the chosen class summand. Extension by zero supplies the common eigenvector of the full finite-dimensional trace space.

claims.title: The weight of a rational similitude on the dual coefficient space
claims.hypotheses: The rational similitude has invertible algebra component of size n with separable minimal polynomial of degree n and nonzero rational multiplier. Pair the embeddings of the CM field and choose nonnegative determinant shifts making the weights polynomial.
claims.statement: The trace of the dual coefficient action equals the product, over all complex embeddings, of the prescribed Schur characters on the roots of the normalized reciprocal polynomial.
